title: Coinduction for a closed section of a flat finitely presented morphism
statement:
Let $p:W\to Z$ be a flat locally finitely presented morphism between quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes, and let $i:Z\hookrightarrow W$ be a closed immersion with $p\circ i=\mathrm{id}_Z$ [def-pc-scheme], [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], [def-weil-flat-morphism], [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Use the unbounded derived categories of structure-module sheaves and their full quasi-coherent subcategories [def-pc-derived-category], derived direct image [def-pc-derived-direct-image], and derived internal Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Let $c$ be a supplied right adjoint to $Ri_*$ on $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}$, with counit $\varepsilon^i$. For $M\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(W)$ assume $H^j(M)=0$ for all $j<n$ for some integer $n$. There is a canonical natural isomorphism
$$\Phi_M:Ri_*c(M)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\mathcal Hom_W(i_*\mathcal O_Z,M).$$
It is normalized so that evaluation at the unit $\mathcal O_W\to i_*\mathcal O_Z$ corresponds to $\varepsilon^i_M$. More precisely, for every $h:\mathcal O_Z\to c(M)$, put $\xi=\varepsilon^i_M\circ Ri_*h:i_*\mathcal O_Z\to M$. Then $\Phi_M\circ Ri_*h$ is the transpose of
$$i_*\mathcal O_Z\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_W}i_*\mathcal O_Z\xrightarrow{m}i_*\mathcal O_Z\xrightarrow{\xi}M.$$
Here $m$ is the canonical derived multiplication induced by the ordinary multiplication on the direct-image algebra, and transpose uses the canonical derived tensor--Hom bijection [def-pc-canonical-derived-tensor-hom-bijection], with the derived tensor structure [def-pc-scheme-derived-tensor-structure]. No Noetherianity, perfectness of $i_*\mathcal O_Z$, or properness of $p$ is assumed.

source.place: Tags 0A9X (lemma-twisted-inverse-image-closed), 0A77 (lemma-sheaf-with-exact-support-ext), and 0E2T (definition-relative-dualizing-complex, following paragraph); the closed section is pseudo-coherent by more-morphisms.tex Tags 0695 (lemma-flat-finite-presentation-pseudo-coherent) and 0683 (lemma-permanence-pseudo-coherent).

proof.text: Put $B=i_*\mathcal O_Z$ and $\mathcal J=\ker(\mathcal O_W\to B)$. First $B[0]$ is pseudo-coherent. Indeed $\mathcal O_Z[0]$ is pseudo-coherent relative to $\mathrm{id}_Z$: on each affine base open use the identity embedding into relative affine space of dimension zero and the one-term rank-one free complex. For every integer $m$ its identity map satisfies the defining $m$-approximation conditions. Apply [lem-sfb-flat-ambient-relative-pseudocoherence] to $Z\xrightarrow{i}W\xrightarrow{p}Z$, using $pi=\mathrm{id}$ and the assumed flatness and local finite presentation of $p$. It gives $Ri_*\mathcal O_Z$ pseudo-coherent. The exactness supplied by [lem-pc-closed-module-pushforward-homology] identifies this object with $B[0]$, by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor].

Factor ordinary $i_*$ as $TE$, where $E:\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_Z)\to\operatorname{Mod}(B)$ is pushforward retaining the $B$-action and $T$ forgets this action. This $E$ is an exact equivalence. To see essential surjectivity explicitly, an arbitrary $B$-module $F$, viewed over $\mathcal O_W$, is killed by $\mathcal J$. The unit quotient formula [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-unit-quotient] gives $F\simeq i_*i^*F$ since $\mathcal JF=0$. This is $B$-linear: $\mathcal O_W\to B$ is a surjection of sheaves, so its local lifts test $B$-linearity. The same test shows that every $\mathcal O_W$-linear map between $B$-modules is $B$-linear. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-pushforward-fully-faithful] gives full faithfulness of $E$. Exactness follows from [lem-pc-closed-module-pushforward-homology], since kernels and cokernels for $B$-modules have the same underlying module sheaves. Choose a quasi-inverse $V$ with these natural unit identifications.

source.place: Section Right adjoint of pushforward for closed immersions, before Tag 0A76; modules.tex Tag 08KS, lemma-i-star-equivalence

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-sheaf-coinduction-adjunction] to $i$. It supplies $H:\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_W)\to\operatorname{Mod}(B)$, $T\dashv H$, and $TH(F)\simeq\mathcal Hom_W(B,F)$ with action $(b\phi)(b')=\phi(bb')$ and counit $\phi\mapsto\phi(1)$, including restriction to smaller opens. Put $C=VH$. Composing the Hom bijection with $E\dashv V$ gives $i_*\dashv C$. Under $i_*C(F)\simeq TH(F)$ its counit is evaluation at $1$. Both $T$ and $E$ are exact: $T$ leaves kernels and sheafified cokernels unchanged, and $E$ is the exact equivalence of Step 2. Consequently $i_*$ is exact, and [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective] shows that $C$ sends K-injective complexes to K-injective complexes.

For any $M\in D(\mathcal O_W)$ take a K-injective representative $I$ using [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist], and define $J(M)=Q_ZC(I)$. For a complex $N$ on $Z$, the ordinary adjunction gives a bijection of chain maps $i_*N\to I$ and $N\to C(I)$. It preserves homotopies: in degree $-1$ the same adjunction intertwines $d_I s+s d_N$, since it is additive and natural in source and target. Pass to homotopy classes and use [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] for $I$ and $C(I)$. This yields $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(W)}(Ri_*N,M)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_{D(Z)}(N,J(M))$, natural in both variables. Thus $Ri_*\dashv J$ on the full unbounded categories, with counit represented by evaluation at $1$. Exactness of $i_*$ and [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor] identify $Ri_*J(M)$ with $Q_W\mathcal Hom_W(B,I)$, which is $R\mathcal Hom_W(B,M)$ by [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Call this natural identification $\Psi_M$.

source.place: Tags 0A76 and 0A77, constructions and proofs; derived.tex Tag 070I, lemma-K-injective

proof.text: Now let $M\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(W)$ have $H^j(M)=0$ for $j<n$. By Step 1 and [lem-sc-rhom-supported-qcoherent], $R\mathcal Hom_W(B,M)$ has quasi-coherent cohomology. Since exact $i_*$ commutes with cohomology, Step 4 gives $i_*H^q(J(M))\simeq H^q(R\mathcal Hom_W(B,M))$. Each is killed by $\mathcal J$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-pushforward-annihilated](2) to this quasi-coherent module. Its pullback is quasi-coherent and is isomorphic to $H^q(J(M))$ by the ordinary counit isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-pushforward-fully-faithful]. Therefore $J(M)\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(Z)$. This uses bounded-below $M$, not perfectness of $B$.

For this $M$, both $c(M)$ and $J(M)$ represent the same functor on all of $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(Z)$: $N\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}_{D(W)}(Ri_*N,M)$. The latter equality uses fullness of the quasi-coherent subcategories and Step 5, not a claim that $J$ preserves every unbounded quasi-coherent object. Define $\alpha_M:c(M)\to J(M)$ to be the $J$-adjunct of $\varepsilon^i_M$, and $\beta_M:J(M)\to c(M)$ the $c$-adjunct of the $J$-counit $e_M$. Then $e_M Ri_*\alpha_M=\varepsilon^i_M$ and $\varepsilon^i_M Ri_*\beta_M=e_M$. Applying the two adjunction bijections gives $\beta_M\alpha_M=1$ and $\alpha_M\beta_M=1$. Naturality follows by applying the same bijection to each square and using counit naturality. Set $\Phi_M=\Psi_M Ri_*\alpha_M$. Evaluation at the unit is represented in Step 4 by $\phi\mapsto\phi(1)$, so the first equation gives exactly the stated counit normalization.

Let $h:\mathcal O_Z\to c(M)$ and $k=\alpha_Mh$. As $C(I)$ is K-injective, [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] represents $k$ by an actual chain map $\mathcal O_Z[0]\to C(I)$. Pushing it forward gives a $B$-linear chain map $g:B[0]\to\mathcal Hom_W(B,I)$. The chain map $\xi_0:B[0]\to I$ obtained by evaluation at $1$ represents $\xi$, by Step 6. On every open and every pair of local sections $b,b'$ of $B$, the action formula in [lem-sc-sheaf-coinduction-adjunction] gives
$$g(b)(b')=(b'g(b))(1)=g(b'b)(1)=\xi_0(bb').$$
These equations are equations of sheaf morphisms, since the cited action formula includes restrictions. Thus ordinary uncurrying of $g$ is ordinary multiplication followed by $\xi_0$.

source.place: Tag 0E2T following paragraph; multiplication-action calculation from modules.tex Tag 0A6F

proof.text: To verify the derived transpose with the fixed normalization, choose a K-flat resolution $q:P\to B[0]$ by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. The composite $gq:P\to\mathcal Hom_W(B,I)$ represents $\Phi_MRi_*h$ after the source identification $QP\simeq B[0]$. The canonical bijection [def-pc-canonical-derived-tensor-hom-bijection] takes it to the chain map $P\otimes B[0]\to I$ given by $x\otimes b\mapsto g(qx)(b)=\xi_0(qx\,b)$. Here only degree-zero $qx$ contributes; the other degrees map to zero, so there is no sign. Under [def-pc-scheme-derived-tensor-structure], $P\otimes B[0]$ represents $B\otimes^{\mathbf L}B$, and $x\otimes b\mapsto qx\,b$ is precisely its canonical derived multiplication (the tensor comparison to $B\otimes B$ followed by ordinary multiplication). The displayed chain map is therefore $\xi\circ m$. This proves the final clause for every $h$.
